## Plan

The only Do‑All blocker for the `i` loop is the RAW on `v`: line 20's write (`v[jv[i]]`) must reach line 19's read (`v[kv[i]]`) of a *later* iteration — a value in transit, so it can be moved but not dropped. Because it's a RAW, the write instance that feeds a given read always occurs earlier in program order, so if every write (line 20) for the whole `i` range runs to completion before any read (line 19) runs, every read still sees exactly the value it originally would have. `u` was not flagged as a blocker: line 19's write locations (`ju[i]`) and line 20's read locations (`ku[i]`) never collide, so reading `u` in a phase before or after the `u[ju[i]] += ...` updates yields the same values.

So I split the body into two full-range loops over the same `i` bounds, keeping line 20 first (its writes) and line 19 second (its reads), instead of interleaving them per iteration. This turns the loop-carried v-dependency into a between-phases dependency (loop 2 wholly after loop 1), leaving neither split loop with a remaining loop-carried dependence. No bounds need to change — both loops still run `i = 1 ..
